name: Shenzhen Snapmaker Technologies Co., Ltd.
summary: Shenzhen company founded 2016, distinctive for building multi-function 3-in-1 machines (3D printing, laser, CNC) rather than printers alone (Snapmaker 2.0, Artisan, J1, U1). Filament is an in-house accessory line with RFID-tagged spools tuned to Snapmaker's own machines, and the material range is narrower than pure filament brands — PLA variants, PETG, ABS, TPU 95A, unfilled and fibre-filled nylon, PVA and a breakaway support, with no confirmed ASA or PC lines. No third-party OEM relationship is documented and the brand is absent from the owner-verified ground-truth table.

product_lines.name: Silk PLA
product_lines.notes: Gloss-additive silk PLA including metallic gold/silver/copper colourways (pigment effect, not metal-powder fill)

product_lines.name: PETG HF
product_lines.notes: High-flow PETG; process delta only, no petg-hf id in catalog

product_lines.name: TPU / TPU 95A HF
product_lines.notes: Snapmaker spec states hardness >= 95 Shore A; the HF variant is the same durometer in a high-flow formulation

product_lines.name: Black Nylon (PA)
product_lines.notes: Unfilled polyamide; specific grade not disclosed, so mapped to the generic pa entry

product_lines.name: PA-CF
product_lines.notes: Carbon-fibre-filled nylon with the base polyamide grade undisclosed in the Luban PA-Fiber guide; no generic pa-cf id exists - reported as a gap

product_lines.name: PA-GF
product_lines.notes: Glass-fibre-filled nylon with the base polyamide grade undisclosed; pa6-gf exists but the PA6 base is unconfirmed, so not mapped - reported as a gap

product_lines.name: Breakaway Support for PLA
product_lines.notes: Mechanical breakaway support polymer, explicitly non-soluble and distinct from PVA; composition undisclosed and no breakaway-support id exists (hips is the ABS-side analogue) - reported as a gap

additional_notes: Standard PLA around $23/kg. Build plates and other consumables are sold under the Materials/accessories collection for the 3-in-1 machines. Roughly ten years in market as of 2026. Whether the filament is extruded in-house or contract-manufactured is unverified; no specific manufacturing facility was identified. Social profiles on YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and X are presumed to exist but were not verified, so none are recorded.

provenance.conflicts: Corporate sourcing is thinner than the other brands in this cluster; founding year rests largely on 3dprintingjournal.com and a Baidu Baike entry. Actual production origin (in-house vs contracted) is unverified, as is the absence of ABS/ASA/PA/PC lines (likely absent rather than confirmed absent).
